_comment: The Jellyfin plugins this deployment runs, pinned. Read by
init/init.py (so a fresh install comes up with them).
Why a pin at all: neither plugin records which build it is. The OIDC
plugin's meta.json ships no sourceUrl, and the LDAP plugin reports an empty
versions list, so before this file the only record of what was installed was
a zip in /tmp - while a rebuilt host either came back with no SSO button or
silently took whatever Jellyfin's catalog and GitHub's `latest` offered.
Both hashes are asserted (the zip, and the assembly inside it, which is what
Jellyfin actually loads), so a swap to a different build is a finding rather
Measured on the media host on 2026-09-18. The LDAP entry also settles a real
outage: LDAP-Auth v23 was still installed beside v24, Jellyfin loaded both,
and every authentication threw InvalidCastException - the login form answered
HTTP 500 for a correct password exactly as it did for a wrong one. The
assembly hash is what catches that coming back.

plugins.name: oidc
plugins.title: OIDC RBAC (the Cerulean Authentik button on Jellyfin's login page)
plugins.provides: the Cerulean Authentik button on Jellyfin's login page, with group-to-library RBAC

plugins.name: ldap
plugins.title: LDAP Authentication (the credential store behind Jellyfin's login page)
plugins.provides: the Authentik LDAP outpost as Jellyfin's credential store, so every account is a Cerulean identity
